data.name: Varun
data.gender_notes: Varun is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root vṛ, 'to cover, encompass' — Varuṇa, the god of waters. Its root is Sanskrit vṛ (वृ). Varuna, the Vedic god of water and cosmic order. Varun is a Sanskrit name meaning “Water; the sea god; all-encompassing”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Varun expresses “Water; the sea god; all-encompassing”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root vṛ, 'to cover, encompass' — Varuṇa, the god of waters.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Varun total 22, reducing to 4. Number 4 is associated with discipline, order and steady effort.

vedic_reference.note: The name Varun is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘वरु’, which is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures including the Rigveda, Mahabharata, and Puranas. The god Varun is considered one of the Adityas, or solar deities, and is also associated with the Vedic god of the sky, Indra.
